answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to radio diffraction telemetry. A node authenticates by measuring phase shifts between an emitter on a knoll and a sensor behind a vine, recording propagation delays at each mesh vertex. An adversary must deploy discrete transceivers across physical terrain per identity, incurring ongoing hardware and land costs. However, seasonal foliage loss shifts baseline RF reflections, occasionally causing false rejections.
